title: Released in installments
summary: The portal's timeline for one request records documents released on three or more separate dates spanning more than 90 days.

sections.heading: What it shows
paragraphs: Each "Document(s) Released" event on a NextRequest timeline (including releases shown only to the requester) is stored with its recorded time, the file names it lists, and the byline it came from. An installment is a calendar date, in the portal's own time, on which at least one release is recorded; several uploads on one day count once. The finding lists every installment date and how many files each listed.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That any deadline was missed. Records may be produced in stages, a requester may agree to a schedule, or a request may be narrowed or added to. The release dates are never used as the agency's determination date, and the timeline does not record why the release was spread out.
A release event that lists no file names is shown as "no files listed", not as zero documents.

sections.heading: Why three dates and 90 days
paragraphs: Measured on 142 San Diego requests about encampments: two release dates are usually one release and one supplement, and the span of multi-date releases jumps from 74 days or less to 132 days or more. The thresholds sit inside that gap.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is not assessed: the finding restates recorded dates and infers nothing to score.
